I have farmed this land for 35 years. I am 54 now, and I never went to school, but I know every corner of my 12 mu. Last year I planted 10 mu with wheat and then maize, and I kept 2 mu for cotton. The wheat gave me about 900 jin per mu, the maize about 1,150 jin, and the cotton about 440 jin. It was an okay year, not great, but we got by.

For the wheat, I start in October. I till the 10 mu with the rotary tiller — I hire Old Zhang's machine for 50 yuan per mu. I buy improved wheat seed from the dealer in town. I put one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on each mu before sowing. That is my base. Then at green-up in spring, I irrigate once from my well. At jointing time, I spread half a bag of urea — 20 jin — on each mu. If the wheat looks yellow, I add a little more, but last year 20 jin was enough. I irrigate two more times, at booting and at grain-filling. So three irrigations total. For spraying, I do herbicide once after sowing, insecticide twice in spring, and fungicide once if it gets damp. That is four times. I would rather spend the money on fertilizer than risk a bad harvest. Last year's amounts worked, so I will do the same.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June. I use hybrid seed — Nongda or something like that — one small package per mu, about 3 jin. I do not till again. I sow directly into the wheat stubble. I put one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing time. When the maize is knee-high, about 20 days later, I top-dress with half a bag of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once at the big trumpet stage and once when the pollen comes out. For bugs and weeds, I spray herbicide once, insecticide three times, and I use a plant regulator once to keep the stalks short. That makes five sprayings. I watch what my neighbors do. If everyone sprays five times, I spray five times too.

For cotton, I keep 2 mu because cotton prices were decent last year. I plow those 2 mu in April with the rotary tiller. I sow improved cotton seed — about 3 jin per mu. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and half a bag of urea when the first flowers open. Cotton drinks more water and the bugs love it. I irrigate three times — at seedling stage, at budding, and at peak flowering. I spray ten times total. Bollworms and aphids never stop. I use insecticide most of those times, herbicide once, and sometimes fungicide if the leaves spot.

I worry about costs. A bag of compound fertilizer is 130 yuan now, and urea is not cheap either. But I will not cut back. Last year I spent the money and we had grain to eat and some to sell. A bad harvest is a disaster. My neighbor Old Wang puts more fertilizer than me, but his son sends money from the city. I have to balance everything — fertilizer, pesticide, hired labor for harvest. If I have 1,000 yuan for inputs, I spend it carefully, but I do not skip what the crop needs. I do what I did before. Change is risky.
